\paragraph{X4: conditional rejection references.}
The oracle direction knows the alternative.
Its critical value was estimated from \resultnum{v4x.x4.sizes.check}{[n]} null \resultplural{v4x.x4.sizes.check}{score}{scores}. The fitted-panel procedure used \resultnum{v4x.x4.sizes.analyst}{[n]} simulated \resultplural{v4x.x4.sizes.analyst}{panel}{panels} per fitting evaluation and \resultnum{v4x.x4.sizes.nulls}{[n]} fresh null \resultplural{v4x.x4.sizes.nulls}{panel}{panels} for its bootstrap.
Tables~\ref{tab:v4x-x4a} and \ref{tab:v4x-x4b} report rejection references, intervals and panel denominators. Table~\ref{tab:v4x-x4-failures} separately reports failures counted as non-rejections and the success-conditioned reference.
The bootstrap p-value formula establishes neither exact validity over the composite null nor an analyst's attainable power.
X4b and its zero-strength calibration reference are declared only at $r\in\{\resultnum{v4.protocol.r.050}{[value]},\resultnum{v4.protocol.r.070}{[value]},\resultnum{v4.protocol.r.090}{[value]}\}$; values outside this domain are not missing in-domain estimates.
